report.source_text: Three days post-admission, the patient was noted to be drowsy and tachypnoeic with a respiratory rate of 22 breaths/min. On examination, the patient was afebrile, oxygen saturation was 97% on normal face mask 5 L /min, with a normal blood pressure and pulse. On examination, the patient appeared lethargic and slightly anxious, with a Glasgow Coma Score of 12; however, he was still able to transfer slowly from armchair to bed independently. It was noted that he was slurring his speech and had an episode of urinary incontinence. Pupils were equal and reactive, however neurological examination could not be performed adequately as the patient was not obeying and following all commands.

clinician.final_diagnosis: severe COVID-19 pneumonia complicated by multiorgan thrombosis including myocardial ischaemia, left ventricular thrombus, intracranial thrombosis and mesenteric involvement despite prophylactic anticoagulation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old man with dyslipidaemia and diabetes presented 7 days after COVID-19 positive test with central compressive pleuritic chest pain, shortness of breath, lethargy and dry cough. Initial ECG showed right heart strain and new right bundle branch block. Chest X-ray revealed diffuse bilateral patchy airspace shadowing consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia. Elevated D-dimer and troponins indicated thrombosis and myocardial injury. Echocardiogram demonstrated a dilated left ventricle with reduced ejection fraction and akinetic walls but no LV thrombus documented. The patient developed neurological decline on ICU day 3 with drowsiness, slurred speech, and reduced GCS. Brain MRI revealed established left temporal and right occipital infarcts with microhemorrhages and sulcal edema, confirming intracranial thrombosis. Abdominal CT angiogram was ordered to evaluate mesenteric thrombosis, though results were not disclosed.

Laboratory tests revealed grossly elevated D-dimer at 5483 ng/mL and markedly elevated troponins indicating thrombosis and myocardial injury
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction of 35% and akinetic apical, anteroseptal and anterior walls, consistent with myocardial ischemia
On ICU day 3, clinical neurological deterioration including drowsiness, slurred speech, urinary incontinence, and lower GCS occurred
Brain MRI on ICU day 3 showed established infarcts in left temporal and right occipital lobes with microhaemorrhagic transformation and sulcal oedema confirming intracranial thrombosis
